subject: Next steps: DataCrest evaluation plan & vendor gap probes
messages:
From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@datacrest.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: DataCrest evaluation plan & vendor gap probes

Hi Emily — thanks again for carving out time today. Short post-call recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum:

TL;DR
- Goal: Validate vendor fit for production inference (latency, cost per request, and data isolation) and confirm quality on your priority prompt set.
- Timeline: 2-week active bakeoff window + 1 week buffer for procurement/contracting.

What we heard (pain points)
- Slow tail latency on existing infra when concurrent requests spike (esp. long-context jobs).
- Unclear unit economics because of bursty usage and internal caching gaps.
- Hard requirement: support for VPC/private deployment + audit logs for governance.

Success metrics (your asks)
1) P95 latency < 350ms on 4k tokens for concurrent 8 qps steady-state
2) Cost per 1k tokens within agreed target band (will verify after quantized run)
3) Audit logs accessible to your SIEM and KMS integration validated

Decision criteria (what DataCrest will weigh)
- Performance (latency percentiles + stability under burst)
- Cost predictability (reserved vs burst economics)
- Security posture (VPC, KMS, SOC2 evidence)
- Operational controls (routing/fallback, rollout tooling)

Open questions / blind spots we flagged
- Which models are in scope on your side (any internal fine-tuned models or only open checkpoints)?
- Exact prompt mix for the quality validation (can you finalize 50 canonical prompts?)
- Procurement lead times and required contract terms (SLA, indemnity thresholds)

Proposed bakeoff tests (owners & quick plan)
- Functional quality: run 50 canonical prompts (DataCrest supplies) against Redwood + CompetitorA + CloudAI Edge. Owner: Emily / DataCrest.
- Latency/stability: 2-hour simulated burst window (8 qps steady, 25 qps burst). Owner: Marcus (Redwood infra).
- Isolation/security: run VPC deploy smoke tests and KMS key rotation. Owner: Marissa (Redwood Security).

Attachments attached: redwood_bakeoff-checklist.xlsx (test matrix), dc_sample_prompts.csv (prompt template), redwood-vs-competitors-matrix.pdf (initial feature map).

Next immediate asks for DataCrest
- Emily: please confirm the 50 canonical prompts by end of week (Fri 10/2).
- Procurement: send any mandatory legal clause list or a redline by 10/6 so we can loop legal.

We’ll set up the shared Drive with test harness instructions and a preliminary schedule — draft is linked below. Happy to adjust scope if you prefer a tighter initial test (e.g., narrow to customer-facing flows only).

Thanks — looking forward to the test window.

—
Lauren Bishop

Thanks Lauren — nice summary. A couple of clarifications from our side that will affect the tests:

1) Prompt set: we will supply 40 canonical prompts this week and 10 additional edge-case prompts (privacy-sensitive redactions) next Tuesday. We want the edge cases included in the quality run but quarantined as a separate bucket for metrics.

2) Models in scope: initially public checkpoints + our small internal tuned model (we'll provide weights access via S3 to vendors under NDA). If Redwood needs an account to pull the tuned model, let us know and we’ll provision temporary credentials.

3) SLA expectations: the procurement team will need an SLA draft with SLOs and an uptime credit table. Procurement is CCed on this thread — Joe, can your team share the SLA template we should be working against?

4) Timeline: the 2-week active window looks fine, tentative start 10/12. Please confirm Redwood's availability for that week (also: we plan a parallel POC with CompetitorA; please note we expect strict parity in test conditions).

One small ask: can Redwood provide a short checklist of the exact telemetry we will receive during the latency run (token-level breakdown, p50/p95/p99, and request traces)? That will help us align our dashboards.

- Infra: we can reserve a dedicated 4-GPU pool for the 10/12 start. I'll put a soft hold on capacity for 10/12-10/23. If DataCrest confirms, we should run a dry run 48 hours prior to validate KV cache priming.

2) Deliverables from DataCrest by 10/02: canonical_prompts_40.csv + edge_prompts_10.csv + access details for tuned model (S3 creds). If you need a one-time signed NDA for S3 access, we can expedite.

4) Contract: Procurement — when you have a redline, please send to lauren.bishop@redwood.com and legal@redwood.com. If helpful, Redwood can share a standard enterprise SOW + SLA template this week.

5) Comparative baseline: we WILL run the following variants to keep parity across vendors:
   - fp16 baseline on public checkpoint
   - 8-bit quantized variant for cost comparison
   - tuned-model run if DataCrest provides access (separate bucket)

6) Next call: let's do a short 30-min kickoff on 10/09 to walk through the test harness and telemetry. Availability window: 9am-12pm PT. Please propose a time and I’ll send a calendar invite.
